title: Schema enforcement canary: traffic mirroring + fallback latency telemetry for constrained decoder
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Create a canary validator that mirrors production streaming requests into a schema-enforcement constrained decoder path, measures schema-failure rates and end-to-end latency delta, and validates fallback behavior for constrained-decoder timeouts and enforced corrections.
background: We have recurring production incidents where strict JSON mode enforcement causes elevated tail latency or partial-stream failures when models emit interleaved tool calls or unexpected tokens. Existing e2e tests exercise many synthetic scenarios, but we lack a lightweight production canary that quantifies real-world schema failure rates and the latency cost of enforcement and remedial fallback logic.
goals: Implement a traffic-mirroring canary that forwards a copy of streaming requests to a constrained-decoder validation path without affecting user-facing responses.
Collect per-request schema verdicts (pass | soft-relax | hard-fail) and precise delta metrics for invocation latency and token throughput.
Validate fallback behaviors: permissive decoder fallback, partial-stream recovery heuristics, and automatic model-variant switching when enforcement cost exceeds thresholds.
Produce dashboards and alerting for schema failure rate, enforcement-induced p99 latency delta, and cost delta for mirrored traffic.
Drive a set of actionable thresholds and remediation playbooks for runtime configuration changes (e.g., relax-schema-for-seq-lt-128).
acceptance_criteria: Canary mirrors 100% of opted traffic to the validator path with zero effect on production responses for mirrored cohort.
Collected metrics exist in observability backend: schema_verdict, enforcement_latency_ms, mirrored_cost_tokens, fallback_triggered (true|false).
Dashboards show p50/p95/p99 enforcement latency delta and schema-failure rate broken out by model, route, and request-size bins.
Automated tests simulate interleaved toolcall, partial JSON emissions, and token-injection adversarial cases with deterministic expected verdicts.
Runbook documented with clear remediation steps and thresholds; on-call can flip mirroring, adjust thresholds, or trigger rollout of permissive config.
technical_design: Add a lightweight validator path in the routing layer: when canary flag is set, create a copy of the incoming streaming session and send it to the constrained-decoder stack with schema enforcement enabled and strict timeout (configurable). Instrument per-token timestamps and KV-cache metrics. The primary path returns normally; the mirrored session is observed and its verdicts and metrics are recorded to a metrics topic and a per-request canary trace assembled asynchronously. Implement a throttling guard so mirrored traffic to constrained-decoder cannot exceed N concurrent sessions per model to avoid resource contention. Provide a shim to trigger permissive fallback simulations: if validator observes hard failures, the shim can simulate fallback flows to ensure fallback logic remains functional. Store canary outputs in long-term object store for batch analysis and offline fuzz correlation. Detailed design doc: https://confluence.redwood-inference.internal/display/INF/Schema+Enforcer+Canary+Design
test_plan: Unit tests for mirror-copy serialization and routing invariants (no user-response mutations).
Integration tests: end-to-end streaming session mirrored to validator with synthetic models that emit known schema states (good, soft-relax, hard-fail).
Load test: mirror rate at 5%, 20%, 50% with concurrency caps to validate system stability and resource isolation.
Fuzz harness: random token-injection into streaming responses to estimate soft-relax heuristics coverage and catch decoder panics.
Canary correctness check: validate that when fallback is triggered in mirrored path, the production path stayed unaffected and fallback metrics are recorded.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal-only opt-in routing for platform team with 1% mirrored traffic for 48 hours to smoke for obvious errors.
Stage 2: Increase to 5% mirrored traffic for 1 week; validate p99 latency delta < 60ms for critical routes or set model-specific exemptions.
Stage 3: 20% mirror for 2 weeks with dashboards and alerts; iterate on heuristics and throttles.
Stage 4: Switch mirror from passive to active advisory mode (automatic suggestions surfaced in Console) and runsideband analysis for one release cycle.
All stages: ensure opt-out and emergency kill-switch available via routing config and runbook.
risks: Mirrored constrained-decoder could consume GPUs and affect production if throttles are misconfigured.
Metrics explosion and high cardinality from per-request traces — must sanitize and sample appropriately.
False positives from soft-relax heuristics may lead to unnecessary config churn; need thresholds tied to customer impact and cost delta.
Privacy: mirrored payloads may include sensitive prompts — ensure mirror obeys PII filter and tenant isolation rules.
